40.title: Praying in the Spirit
40.mainScripture: Romans 8:26–27 — 'Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.'
supportingScriptures: Jude 1:20 — 'But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost.'
1 Corinthians 14:4 — 'He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.'
Ephesians 6:18 — 'Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints.'

1 Corinthians 14:14–15 — 'For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful. What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also: and I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.'
40.reality:
One of the most underused gifts of the new birth is the capacity to pray in the Spirit—to allow the Holy Spirit to pray through your spirit, bypassing the limitations of your natural mind. Your mind doesn't always know what to pray. Your spirit, joined to God's Spirit, always does.

Romans 8:26 says the Spirit 'helps our infirmities'—our weaknesses, limitations, not-knowing. When you don't know how to pray, when you're overwhelmed, when you've run out of words, the Spirit prays through you according to the perfect will of God.
40.important:
Praying in the Spirit is not a second-tier experience for 'special' Christians. It's a resource given to every believer for the strengthening of their spirit and the building of their inner man. 1 Corinthians 14:4 says it 'edifies'—builds up, strengthens—you personally.

A believer who prays in the Spirit regularly builds herself up in the inner man. The spirit grows stronger. The mind is renewed. The capacity for faith increases. This is not a substitute for understanding-based prayer—it complements it. Together, they cover what no single mode of prayer could cover alone.

41.title: Releasing Your True Identity
41.mainScripture: Ephesians 1:3–4 — 'Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love.'
supportingScriptures: Romans 8:37 — 'Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.'
1 John 4:17 — 'Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world.'
2 Corinthians 2:14 — 'Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.'
Colossians 1:27 — 'To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.'
41.reality:
Your true identity is not your background, your failures, your family history, or your natural abilities. Your true identity is who you are in Christ—chosen before the foundation of the world, blessed with all spiritual blessings, destined for glory. This is not who you are working toward. This is who you already are.

The entire 100-day journey is really about this: releasing your true identity. Not acquiring something new, but removing the false layers—shame, fear, self-condemnation, religious performance—that have covered over who you actually are in Christ.
41.important:
Most of life's limitations come not from lacking resources but from failing to know and occupy your true identity. The woman who knows she is chosen, blessed, holy, and more than a conqueror will live differently—speak differently, decide differently, relate differently—than the woman who still identifies with her failures and lacks.

'As he is, so are we in this world.' Not after we die. Not when we're more mature. In this world. Now. Your identity is already fully established in the spirit. Release it. Let it govern your soul. Let it be seen in your body and your life.

42.title: Mind Your Spirit
42.mainScripture: Colossians 3:2 — 'Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.'
supportingScriptures: Philippians 4:8 — 'Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.'
Isaiah 26:3 — 'Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.'
Romans 8:6 — 'For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.'
Proverbs 4:23 — 'Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.'
42.reality:
'Mind your spirit' is perhaps the single most practical instruction for the Christian life. What you set your mind on is what grows strong. What grows strong is what governs your life. If you set your mind on problems, fear, and failure—those grow strong. If you set your mind on spiritual realities—peace, identity, provision, victory—those grow strong.

The soul is the battleground. Satan cannot touch your spirit. He cannot un-save you. But he can wage war in your soul—putting thoughts in your mind, stirring emotions, creating spiritual doubt—hoping to separate you in practice from the realities your spirit already holds.
42.important:
'Set your affection'—the word is phroneoite, meaning to have the mindset, to think about deliberately, to orient yourself toward. This is not passive. You choose what you set your mind on. You have to actively redirect your thoughts from earthly things to heavenly realities.

The practice: throughout your day, when your mind drifts to anxiety, comparison, or fear, consciously redirect it. 'What is true about me in Christ? What is true about God? What is He doing in this?' This is not denial. This is minding your spirit—keeping the inner life in top condition so it can govern the outer life well.

43.title: Time to Leave!—Living with Eternal Perspective
43.mainScripture: Philippians 1:21–23 — 'For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain. But if I live in the flesh, this is the fruit of my labour: yet what I shall choose I wot not. For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better.'
supportingScriptures: 2 Corinthians 5:6–8 — 'Therefore we are always confident, knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:) We are confident, I say, and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.'
Romans 8:18 — 'For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.'
1 Corinthians 2:9 — 'But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.'

Revelation 21:4 — 'And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.'
43.reality:
The entire Spirit, Soul & Body series arrives at this: you are not primarily a physical being having a spiritual experience. You are a spirit being having a temporary physical experience. This body is not your permanent home. This earth is not your final destination.

Paul says 'to die is gain' because he understood that to leave the body is to be fully present with Christ—no longer operating through the limited lens of soul and body, but face to face. The death of the body releases the spirit into its fullest expression.
43.important:
This eternal perspective changes everything about how you live. When you know this is temporary, you don't cling to earthly things too tightly. You use them, steward them, enjoy them—but you're not dependent on them. Your joy isn't at the mercy of circumstances, because your real life is hidden with Christ in God (Colossians 3:3).

This is the graduation of the spirit-soul-body understanding: your spirit is your primary reality. Your soul is being renewed to agree with that reality. Your body is serving that reality for a season. And when the body is done, the spirit goes to its origin—not with dread, but with anticipation, because what awaits is 'far better.'
